haiku-low.q1: Keys load at process start, before the HTTP server serves traffic. /healthz returns 503 until all three keys are in the snapshot, then 200.
haiku-low.q2: It retries (4 attempts total, 2 seconds apart), logs an error without values, and exits non-zero. It never turns ready, so with maxUnavailable 0 the rollout halts and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: A background timer re-reads each secret every 5 minutes plus jitter and swaps in a new snapshot atomically. If a read fails, that secret keeps its last good value, a warning is logged, and the next cycle retries.
haiku-low.q4: Key values live only in process memory, in the snapshot. They must never appear in environment variables, on disk, or in logs. Version ids may be logged.
haiku-low.q5: Only the security on-call group can write orders-api/prod/*. The orders-api-prod identity can read it. Engineers have no read access to prod.
haiku-low.q6: The old keys remain in git history and pre-migration images. They become harmless only when revoked at the provider, which is rollout step 7.
haiku-low.q7: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__. At each call they read the current snapshot (for example secrets.get('payments_api_key')) and build the Authorization header.
haiku-low.q8: In the metrics service, all 4 pods must show the version ids recorded in step 3. The pod list must show no pre-migration image. Then wait 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access (step 1), copy new keys into the store (step 3), switch the app and remove config keys in one merge (step 4), then revoke old provider keys (step 7).
haiku-low.q10: make run reads orders-api/dev/* sandbox keys using the engineer's own identity. make run-offline uses a stub backend and fake servers, needing no keys.
haiku-low.q11: It retries the load (4 attempts total), then logs an error without values and exits non-zero. It never turns ready, even though two secrets loaded.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at process start, before the HTTP server serves traffic. /healthz returns 503 until the snapshot holds all three keys, then 200.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 try + 3 retries, 2s apart), then logs an error without values and exits non-zero. It never turns ready. With maxUnavailable: 0 the rollout halts, old pods keep serving, and a progress deadline raises an alert. Live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer re-reads every secret 5 minutes after the last attempt (plus jitter). It copies the snapshot, replaces the secrets read successfully, and swaps the copy in atomically. If a read fails, that secret keeps its last good value, a warning with the name and error type is logged, and the next cycle retries with a fresh token. Stale-key alert fires if over 15 minutes stale.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory, in the in-memory snapshot (a map of name to (value, version_id)). They must never be in environment variables, on disk, or in logs (version ids may be logged). Core dumps are disabled and the Authorization header is redacted in HTTP debug logging.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call group. Engineers have no read on prod.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED why deletion alone is insufficient in so many words, but the doc says the old keys are leaked in git history and in pre-migration images. The old values are made harmless by revoking them at the providers (after confirming idle), and by deleting pre-migration images from the registry and deploy pipeline list.
sonnet.q7: The client no longer copies the key in __init__. At each call it reads the key from the current snapshot (e.g. secrets.get('payments_api_key')) and builds the Authorization header. In-flight calls keep the value already read.
sonnet.q8: In rollout step 5: in the metrics service, check all 4 pods show the version ids recorded in step 3; check the pod list that no pod runs a pre-migration image; wait 10 minutes (two refresh intervals) to see if any pod picks up a different version. Then step 6 checks the old keys show no provider traffic for at least 30 minutes.
sonnet.q9: Store access/policies and test them (step 1, with the empty prod paths and sandbox keys); build the code change that reads from the store and removes the api_key lines, test in staging (step 2, PR not yet merged); create new provider keys and write them to the prod store (step 3); merge and roll out to prod (step 4); confirm pods (5); check old keys idle (6); revoke old keys (7). So: access, then switch-the-app code built (unmerged), then new keys created and copied into the store, then merge (app switches and committed-file lines are removed), then revoke old keys.
sonnet.q10: make run reads orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys) from the store with the engineer's own identity. make run-offline uses a stub backend and fake local provider servers, needing no store or keys.
sonnet.q11: It retries (4 attempts total, 2s apart). If a secret is still unavailable, it logs an error without values and exits non-zero, and never turns ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. The rotation schedule is an undecided open question; the plan sets no cadence.
